title: Dataverse: create agent users with Microsoft Entra agent identity
summary: Hold: the API entries omit information required to perform the operations they advertise. In particular, selecting all agent identities is not sufficient to create a blocking Conditional Access policy; the request also needs target resources, a block grant and a policy state. The roadmap facts and the distinction between launched status and preview documentation are supported.

claims.claim: The printed PATCH entry is a complete call for changing environment auditing through isauditenabled.
claims.quote:
Change the column values in the organization table to change how auditing works for the environment.

PATCH [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/organizations([Organization ID]) HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/json
claims.fix: Replace the explanatory tail with a concrete request body: PATCH [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/organizations([Organization ID]) with Content-Type: application/json and JSON body {"isauditenabled":true}. The existing method and endpoint are correct, but without a value-bearing body the entry cannot turn auditing on. Retain the current documentation URL.

claims.claim: The printed POST endpoint alone is a complete call to create an Entra agent identity.
claims.quote:
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/serviceprincipals/Microsoft.Graph.AgentIdentity
OData-Version: 4.0
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <token>
{"displayName": "My Agent Identity","agentIdentityBlueprintId": "<my-agent-blueprint-id>","sponsors@odata.bind":
claims.fix: Keep the endpoint but supply the documented request details: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/serviceprincipals/Microsoft.Graph.AgentIdentity with Authorization: Bearer <token>, OData-Version: 4.0, Content-Type: application/json and JSON body {"displayName":"<agent-name>","agentIdentityBlueprintId":"<blueprint-app-id>","sponsors@odata.bind":["https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users/<sponsor-user-id>"]}. The endpoint and beta version are supported; the bodyless request is not sufficient.

claims.claim: POSTing a Conditional Access policy with only conditions.clientApplications.includeAgentIdServicePrincipals set to All supplies a call that blocks token issuance.
claims.fix: Replace the API text with: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/identity/conditionalAccess/policies with Content-Type: application/json and JSON body {"displayName":"Block all agent identities from accessing resources","conditions":{"clientApplications":{"includeAgentIdServicePrincipals":["All"],"excludeAgentIdServicePrincipals":[],"agentIdServicePrincipalFilter":null},"applications":{"includeApplications":["All"],"excludeApplications":[]}},"grantControls":{"operator":"AND","builtInControls":["block"]},"state":"enabledForReportingButNotEnforced"}. Add to the existing note: 'This creates a report-only policy; it does not block until enabled after reviewing its impact.' The cited article recommends report-only first.
